corrections.title: Python heredoc edit script pastes a docstring INCLUDING its own closing triple-quote, ending the script's own literal early and leaving the tail as bare code (SyntaxError)
corrections.cause:
A `python3` heredoc edit script pasted a docstring into its `old = """..."""` literal together with the docstring's OWN closing `"""`, ending that literal early and leaving the script tail as bare top-level code.

REPRODUCED, not inferred (CPython 3.13.9, base c800c2e1e7, archived records 616/617 of session fbd7b22b-949a-4047-8087-6a719edb1dc2). Feeding the archived script back to `python3 -` verbatim reproduces the founding traceback byte for byte.

THE REPORTED SYMPTOM IS NOT THE CAUSE, AND IS NOT STABLE. Control A replaced all ten U+2014 characters in the script with ASCII hyphens and changed nothing else: it still fails, and it fails with a DIFFERENT message, `SyntaxError: unterminated string literal (detected at line 22)`. An ASCII-only recurrence of this exact defect therefore reports a different error string, and a title keyed to the original message would not match it. That is why this entry is no longer titled after the character the interpreter happened to name first.

THE EMBEDDED DELIMITER IS THE CAUSE. Two controls remove it by different routes, each leaving every U+2014 in place, and each returns rc=0 and prints `ok`: control C escapes the offending line to `\"\"\"`, control D deletes it outright.

THE DISCRIMINATOR. The same three characters appear twice in one 50-line Bash command (48 lines reach `python3` once the heredoc wrapper is stripped): RAW as `    """` at line 14, inside the `old` literal, and correctly ESCAPED as `    \"\"\"` at line 25, inside `new`. Eleven lines apart, same script, same author. The raw one is a verbatim copy of the closing delimiter of the docstring being replaced (the pasted excerpt runs to `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py`'s own `    """`). So the defect is a paste that took one line too many, NOT an author who did not know the escaping rule: the correct spelling is already present in the same script.

NOT THE SKIM-REWRITE UMBRELLA (`entry-cand-20260722-6`). That entry's mechanism flattens a Bash command by collapsing every newline to a single space, so a SyntaxError under it could only ever be reported at line 1; this founding traceback reports `File "<stdin>", line 16`, and the archived command still carries its 50 real newlines. Separately, that umbrella's own published discriminator requires the command's FIRST LINE to carry `git status`, `git log`, or `cat`/`head -N` on a source path; this command's first line is `python3 - <<'PYEOF'` and carries none of them. The entry fails the umbrella's test on both limbs, so recurrences of THIS mechanism belong here and not there.

NOT THE HARNESS, THE HEREDOC OR THE DELIVERY PATH. The cause is agent-authored script text. The same bytes reach `python3` intact either way, which is exactly what the surviving newlines above establish.

COST. The agent self-corrected 27 seconds later (records 621/622), re-issuing the same edit with `'''` delimiters over a narrowed excerpt that no longer reached the docstring's closer, and it printed `ok`. The transcript changed both things at once, so it does not by itself isolate which one mattered; controls C and D do, and show that removing the embedded delimiter alone suffices. The cost here is turns, not outcomes.

SCOPE. No agent-facing prompt rule is filed from this entry: that surface is held by sibling task 5683.
corrections.note:
Replaces this entry's title and supplies its first `cause`.

The previous title read "Python heredoc edit script hits a stray unicode em-dash outside its triple-quoted string, raising a SyntaxError". That framing is withdrawn as refuted by measurement rather than by opinion: control A strips every U+2014 from the failing script and it still fails, with a different error. With no `cause` on the entry, that title was the ENTIRE matching key `scripts/legibility/coder.py::build_codebook_index` rendered to the nightly coder, so a recurrence whose error string differed had nothing to match on and would arrive as a fresh candidate.

The 2026-09-19 `fbd7b22b-949a-4047-8087-6a719edb1dc2` sighting is ANNOTATED, not retracted. The symptom it recorded was real and its `evidence_quote` stays exactly as filed; only the explanation it was filed under was wrong.

`status` stays `open`. The defect is live and unfixed; this correction replaces an explanation, it does not retire an entry.

Reproduction: archived transcript records 616 (the Bash `tool_use`), 617 (the `is_error` result), and 621/622 (the +27s self-correction and its `ok`), 0-indexed into the 687-record session archive under task 5580. Four controls were run on CPython 3.13.9 at HEAD c800c2e1e7, each feeding the script to `python3 -` against a throwaway copy of the target file so no tracked file was written: REPRO verbatim (rc=1, stderr byte-identical to record 617); A, every U+2014 to ASCII `-` (rc=1, `unterminated string literal (detected at line 22)`); C, the embedded delimiter escaped (rc=0, `ok`); D, the embedded delimiter deleted (rc=0, `ok`). The control target was located by content and its index asserted to be 14 before perturbation.
